answer: Escrowed Identity Delay. Each new agent identity must lock a fixed deposit plus pay a per-cycle holding fee for a mandatory wait before it can transact; funds sit in escrow through the delay nadir, when fees peak. Cloning n identities costs n times that fee plus locked capital, all forfeited if the identity aborts, making each marginal clone strictly negative-EV. Operators can recycle a relic identity only by repaying the full delay, and the fee schedule is published in shale-like immutable append-only logs auditors can verify.
